verdict.rationale: Requesty documents gateway routing policies that switch models automatically. Fallback Policies retry the next model in a chain when one fails (availability), Load Balancing distributes requests across models by weight, and Latency-Based Routing picks the fastest model from real-time data. The evidence does not show routing rules keyed on cost or on task capability, so only the availability part of the story's policy triggers is clearly covered. missing for 10: documented cost-based routing rules, capability/task-based model selection rules, independent or hands-on corroboration of mid-task switching.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my agent can switch models mid-task by policy — cost, capability, or availability — through gateway routing rules

citations.quote: Fallback Policies automatically retry your requests with different models if one fails
If it fails (timeout, rate limit, error, etc.), the router immediately tries the next model in the chain.
Load Balancing Policies distribute your requests across multiple models based on weights you define.
Latency-Based Routing automatically selects the fastest model for each request based on real-time performance data.
